name: Athens
hook: The city-state Jeopardy loves: Acropolis, Marathon and the war with Sparta.

facts.label: the Acropolis
facts.statement: The Acropolis is the elevated citadel of Athens; its name comes from Greek words meaning "highest city."

facts.label: the Parthenon
facts.statement: The Parthenon is the temple to Athena on the Acropolis; Pericles had it built, and the Elgin Marbles came from its pediments.

facts.label: Marathon
facts.statement: At Marathon in 490 B.C. the Athenians beat the Persians, and a messenger ran roughly 25 miles to Athens with the news.

facts.label: the Peloponnesian War
facts.statement: Sparta defeated Athens in the Peloponnesian War, which ended in 404 B.C. and closed Athens' Golden Age.

facts.label: Socrates
facts.statement: Socrates was convicted in Athens in 399 B.C. of impiety and corrupting the young, and was put to death.

facts.label: Plato's Academy
facts.statement: Plato, a student of Socrates, founded the Academy in Athens around 387 B.C.

facts.label: "The School of Athens"
facts.statement: Raphael's fresco "The School of Athens," painted in the Vatican, gathers the ancient Greek philosophers in one scene.
